issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path; troubleshooting for failed renewals, expired certificates, CA downtime, or root rotation is only touched on briefly.
Examples are prose descriptions of commands rather than runnable end-to-end demonstrations with realistic output, and Example 2 largely points back to Step 5.

scenarios.name: private-ca-init-and-renewal
scenarios.rationale: Both cover the rubric's init, bootstrap with fingerprint, certificate and renew --daemon --exec commands, but A leaves the init password and step-ca start loosely specified, while B gives a complete, concrete flow with --password-file at init and run time, a systemd unit, and a verification step, though its extra provisioner/--not-after details add some risk.

scenarios.name: mtls-orders-to-payments
scenarios.rationale: A uses `step ca certificate` for separate server and client certs, sets requestCert/rejectUnauthorized with the CA root as `ca`, uses curl --cacert/--cert/--key, and notes that a missing client cert fails the handshake (exit 56), which covers nearly the whole rubric. B gets the Node server, curl call and handshake-failure note right but issues the certificates with openssl instead of `step ca certificate`, which misses a key rubric item.

scenarios.name: acme-clients-and-expired-cert-recovery
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric more closely: it uses the `https://ca.corp.internal/acme/acme/directory` URL, says renewal needs the current unexpired cert, tells you to reissue with `step ca certificate`, and suggests a daemon or systemd timer. A also covers most of this but uses a different host and port, and it suggests an `allowRenewalAfterExpiry` claim that it says to verify and that weakens security, which makes it less reliable.
